name: Greenbone (OpenVAS)
author: Netlens
description: Shows what a Greenbone / OpenVAS vulnerability scanner found on your devices: every finding with its severity, CVE numbers, score, the port and the advice of the scanner. Netlens matches each finding to a device by address, warns about new critical vulnerabilities and lists the devices at risk. Read-only: it only asks for results, it never starts a scan.

info.title: Give Netlens a read-only user and reach the scanner
info.text: Netlens talks to the Greenbone Management Protocol (GMP) over TLS, normally on port 9390 of the gvmd service. In the Greenbone Community Containers gvmd only listens on a Unix socket: add a TLS listener (gvmd --listen=0.0.0.0 --port=9390) or put a small TLS proxy in front, and keep that port reachable from Netlens only. In Greenbone (Administration > Users) make a user with the role 'Observer' (it can read results but not change anything), and in every scan task put that user under Observers (Edit task): a user only sees the tasks that are shared with it. For the certificate of gvmd fill in its SHA-256 fingerprint: Netlens then trusts exactly that certificate.

columns.label: Certificate fingerprint
columns.help: SHA-256 fingerprint of gvmd's certificate. When filled in, exactly that certificate is trusted (gvmd makes its own); when empty the certificate is checked the normal way (see 'Verify TLS certificate').

options.label: Everything with a severity above 0 (low and up)

config.label: Minimum quality of detection (%)
config.help: How sure the scanner is about a finding. 70 is what Greenbone itself shows by default; lower values add more guesses.

config.label: Ignore findings older than (days)
config.help: Findings from a scan that is older than this are left out, so a host that was fixed and not scanned again does not stay red for ever.

config.label: Verify TLS certificate
config.help: Only used for a server without a fingerprint. gvmd uses a certificate of its own CA by default, so this is off by default.
